title: CI/CD pipeline & environments
body:
## Context
R0's second goal is blunt: *"Make the pipeline real: a commit to `main` builds, tests, scans, and deploys to dev with no manual step"* (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.1). Every other epic assumes the gates in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§7 (required checks, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. a code-owner) exist and actually block. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` already decided the *shape* - GitHub Actions, path-filtered parallel jobs, a self-hosted runner for GPU benchmarks, Turborepo/uv caching, image-based immutable deploys. This epic **builds** it.

E03 sits on the critical path: the roadmap graph (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§11.1) has `E02 --> E03`, `E03 --> E04` and `E03 --> E09` - observability and auth cannot ship before the pipeline they ship through exists. E03 also owns one of the three mandatory R0 STRIDE models (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4: *"STRIDE models complete for E03 (supply chain), E08 (exchange boundary), E09 (auth/RBAC)"*), because CI is the highest-leverage supply-chain surface in the repository (threat boundary TB-8, `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§5).

E03 has **no user-story domain** (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§2 epic table lists domains "-" for E03): it delivers engineering infrastructure, so its children are Tasks, a Spike, design tickets for the developer-facing surfaces it creates, QA tickets that verify the gates really gate, and security tickets for the supply chain.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pipeline skeleton**: `dorny/paths-filter` change detection, the job matrix, a *required-checks resolver* job (ADR-0013 rule 2), concurrency groups, least-privilege `permissions:` blocks, SHA-pinned actions (SR-132). -> `E03-T01`
- **Language lanes**: JS (eslint, `tsc`, vitest, build, Turborepo remote cache) and Python (ruff, `mypy --strict`, pytest, uv cache) over the E02 layout `packages/chart-engine`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/ui`, `apps/app-web`, `apps/app-electron`, `services/api`. -> `E03-T02`, `E03-T03`
- **Coverage gate**: >=85% backend & engine packages, >=80% frontend, build fails below (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4). -> `E03-T04`
- **Generated-code freshness gate**: `packages/protocol` regenerated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema of `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; any diff fails (ADR-0013 rule 3). -> `E03-T05`
- **Upper pyramid layers**: contract, integration (recorded fixtures only - never `api.bybit.com`, ADR-0012), `e2e-web`, `e2e-electron`, `a11y-axe`. -> `E03-T06`
- **Security lane**: CodeQL, Semgrep (incl. the `cv-*` rules of `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.2), Bandit, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks, license-scan (SR-136 allowlist), Trivy. -> `E03-T07`, `E03-X02`
- **Supply-chain release path**: container build + GHCR push tagged `semver+sha`, CycloneDX SBOM (syft, SR-133), cosign signature + provenance attestation (SR-137). -> `E03-T08`
- **Environments**: dev auto-deploy on every merge to `main`; staging (demo) deploy behind a GitHub Environment with required reviewers; documented rollback (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§9). -> `E03-T09`
- **Migrations**: Alembic job with `alembic heads` == 1 and `alembic check` drift detection (`21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§9), expand/contract assertion (ADR-0013 rule 9). -> `E03-T10`
- **Release automation**: release-please-style changelog job appending to `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3). -> `E03-T11`
- **Branch protection & merge queue as code**: the required-check set from `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3, linear history, no force-push, signed release tags. -> `E03-T13`
- **Security lane rules**: the `cv-*` Semgrep corpus and CodeQL suite are consumed by `E03-T07`; authoring them is deferred (see Deferred scope).
- **Governance artefacts**: CI runbook and the ADR-0013 validation exercises. -> `E03-T15`
- **Gate verification & QA sign-off**: a negative fixture proving every required check actually blocks, plus the epic-level regression pass. -> `E03-Q01`

## Deferred scope (rebaselined to the roadmap budget)
`30-release-roadmap.md` §2 allocates E03 **42 points across the S01-S03 train window**. The first pass of this backlog
sized 82 points and scheduled five children into Sprint 04, outside the window. Rather than silently overrun the agreed
train allocation, E03 is rebaselined to **46 points, all inside S01-S03** (+9.5%, within the +-15% planning tolerance);
the residual 4 points are the re-sizing of `E03-T06` and `E03-Q01` after they shed the work listed below.

The following work is **deferred out of E03** and carried as separate `Backlog` items to be pulled into an R1 train
(a follow-on CI/CD hardening epic) once R0's exit criteria are met. None of it is required by an R0 exit criterion:

| Deferred | Why it can wait past R0 | Re-entry trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `E03-K01` Spike: GPU runner isolation | Engine benchmarks belong to E06/E11, which start in R1. | Before E06 needs a benchmark gate. |
| `E03-T14` GPU benchmark job + baseline | Same; ADR-0013 rule 4 has no R0 consumer. | With `E03-K01`. |
| `E03-T12` Nightly scheduled matrix | Every slot's owner (load, soak, chaos, DAST, a11y sweep) is itself deferred or in a later epic; an all-stub scheduler is cost without signal. | When >=2 slots have real content. |
| `E03-Q02` k6/Locust perf harness | Budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` need a real API/WS surface (E08/E09) to measure. | R1, with E08. |
| `E03-Q03` Pipeline chaos + flaky quarantine | Needs deploy history to quarantine against; manual flake triage is acceptable for one train. | After 1 train of flake data. |
| `E03-Q05` a11y CI harness validation | `E03-T06` ships the harness; there is no product UI to scan until E05. | With E05. |
| `E03-X02` Custom `cv-*` Semgrep rules | `E03-T07` runs the default CodeQL/Semgrep suites in R0; the bespoke corpus targets code (OMS, auth) that does not exist yet. | With E09. |
| `E03-X03` CI secrets/permissions audit | The controls are *implemented* under `E03-X01`'s STRIDE model in R0; the independent audit is the verification pass. | R1 hardening. |
| `E03-X04` ZAP DAST integration | No authenticated surface exists before E09. | With E09. |
| `E03-X05` Security sign-off on signing/SBOM | `E03-T08` DoD keeps the security-engineer review inline; the standalone sign-off ticket duplicated it. | Pre-R4 live-enablement gate. |
| `E03-D01`/`E03-D02` Pipeline-experience design | E03 ships no product screen; failure-message quality is captured as a DoD line on `E03-T01`/`E03-T15` instead of a design-ahead pair. | If CI messaging becomes a measured pain point. |

Work **retained** because an R0 exit criterion or a mandatory gate depends on it: the STRIDE model (`E03-X01`,
`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4), every blocking PR gate (`T01`-`T08`, `T10`, `T13`), dev/staging deploy (`T09`),
release automation (`T11`), the runbook (`T15`) and gate verification + QA sign-off (`Q01`).

## Out of scope
- Kubernetes/cloud orchestration - targets are docker compose on WSL Ubuntu, later a single VPS (`00-planning-brief.md`).
- Terraform/IaC modules - ADR-0013 states "terraform-free (n/a)".
- The observability stack itself (Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager exporters, dashboards, alert routing) - that is **E04**, which depends on E03.
- Authoring engine benchmarks B1-B10 (`26-chart-engine-design.md` Ã‚Â§13) - E03 provides the runner and the comparison harness only; the benchmarks belong to E06/E11.
- Pen-test execution and the Live-enablement gate (R4 / E43, `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§6).
- Android/mobile build lanes - Android is out of scope per the owner decision of 2026-09-14.
- Any product UI: E03 ships no application screen from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Everything in the Deferred scope table above - it is out of E03 and must not be pulled in without a roadmap change to the 42-point allocation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fast, complete signal on a pull request
  Given a pull request touching "services/api" and "packages/protocol"
  When the pipeline runs
  Then the Python lane, contract, integration, generated-code freshness and security jobs execute
  And the chart-engine GPU benchmark job is reported not-applicable by the required-checks resolver
  And end-to-end PR feedback completes within 15 minutes at p90

Scenario: A commit to main reaches dev with no manual step
  Given a pull request is merged to "main" through the merge queue
  When the post-merge workflow completes
  Then an image tagged "<semver>+<sha>" is pushed to GHCR with a CycloneDX SBOM and a cosign signature
  And the dev docker compose stack is redeployed to that exact image digest automatically
  And the deploy smoke test against /health/live, /health/ready and build-info passes

Scenario: A drifted generated protocol cannot merge
  Given a pull request edits "docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml" without regenerating "packages/protocol"
  When the freshness job runs "make gen && git diff --exit-code"
  Then the job fails and the pull request is not mergeable

Scenario: Staging promotion requires a human
  Given a green build on "main"
  When the staging deploy workflow is triggered
  Then it pauses on the "staging" GitHub Environment awaiting a required reviewer
  And no deployment happens until an authorised reviewer approves

Scenario: The supply-chain gate blocks a prohibited licence
  Given a pull request adds a dependency licensed AGPL-3.0
  When the license-scan job evaluates it against the SR-136 allowlist
  Then the job fails and names the offending package in the log
```

## Technical notes / design
- Workflows in `.github/workflows/`: `pr.yml` (matrix entry point), `main.yml` (build/sign/deploy-dev), `staging.yml` (gated deploy), `nightly.yml`, `release.yml`, plus reusable `_job-*.yml` workflows so lanes are composed, not copy-pasted.
- The required-checks resolver is a terminal job reading the paths-filter outputs and each lane's `result`, emitting a single `ci-required` conclusion; it is the only aggregate check in branch protection, so a skipped-but-inapplicable job never wedges the queue while a skipped-but-applicable job fails it.
- Every `uses:` is pinned to a full commit SHA, with a Dependabot `github-actions` ecosystem entry to bump them (SR-132, SR-134).
- Caching: Turborepo remote cache, `uv` cache keyed on `uv.lock`, Playwright browser cache keyed on version, Docker layer cache.
- Deployment is image-based and immutable (rule 8); rollback = redeploy the previous tag, never a down-migration (rule 9).

## Test plan
- Every child carries its own tests. At epic level, verification is the **pipeline verification test plan** (`E03-Q01`) driven by deliberate-failure fixtures: drifted protocol, planted synthetic secret, prohibited licence, coverage drop, unpinned action, Critical Trivy finding, unsigned image, second Alembic head.
- The R0 exit criterion "green pipeline from commit to dev deployment <= 15 min" is measured and recorded by `E03-Q01`.

## Security notes
- The STRIDE model for supply-chain boundary TB-8 is a blocking R0 quality gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4) and is delivered by `E03-X01`.
- Binding controls: SR-130 locked deps, SR-131 digest-pinned non-root base images, SR-132 SHA-pinned actions and least-privilege permissions with `pull_request_target` prohibited, SR-133 SBOM, SR-136 licence policy, SR-137 CI-only signed builds, SR-138 `--ignore-scripts`, SR-140 **no production Bybit credentials in CI ever**, SR-141 OIDC over long-lived tokens plus environment protection, SR-142 gitleaks, SR-146 no secret leakage into CI logs.
- Data classification: CI holds no customer data and no exchange credentials; it holds signing material and registry tokens (Secret/High).

## Accessibility notes
E03 ships no product UI, so WCAG 2.2 AA conformance does not apply to its own output. It owns the **enforcement mechanism**: the `a11y-axe` required check and the nightly `pa11y-ci` sweep on which every UI epic depends (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). Developer-facing artefacts (runbook, failure-triage guide, status surfaces) follow the plain-language, heading-structure and colour-independence rules of `05-accessibility-standard.md` - CI status must never be conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
- Pipeline budget: **p90 PR feedback <= 15 minutes** (ADR-0013 rule 5, R0 exit criterion 2), measured weekly; a breach triggers a matrix rebalance.
- E03 provides the harnesses enforcing the product budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (#3 WS tick->screen, #4 order submit->ack, #5 24 h ingestion soak, #13 REST p95) and the >10% regression rule on engine benchmarks B1-B10.

## Observability
- Workflow-level: job duration and outcome exported into a CI metrics summary; flaky retries recorded (three in a week auto-opens a quarantine issue, ADR-0013 rule 10).
- Deploy-level: each deploy emits an annotated event (image digest, git sha, actor, environment) that E04's Grafana consumes once it exists.
- Audit: environment-approval events for staging promotion are retained in the GitHub audit log and referenced in the release checklist.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 2 demonstrated end-to-end and timed (<= 15 min p90 over a sprint of real PRs).
- [ ] Required status checks of `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 configured and demonstrably blocking (a deliberately failing PR shown unmergeable).
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] CI runbook merged and linked from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: failure triage, benchmark-runner override, rollback, secret rotation.
- [ ] ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Validation satisfied: the deliberate "break the protocol" PR failed the freshness gate, evidence recorded.
- [ ] QA sign-off from `E03-Q01`; PRR-lite item "dev environment rebuild runbook" green.
- [ ] Developer-facing failure messaging reviewed against `E03-T01`'s summary spec and the `E03-T15` runbook (no separate design ticket: E03 ships no product UI; the design-ahead pair is deferred).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at a Sprint Review: a live failing gate and a live dev deploy.

## Dependencies
- **E02** monorepo scaffold & toolchain - the pipeline runs the commands E02 defines (`make gen`, workspace lint/type/test entry points); without the workspace layout there is nothing to path-filter.
- **E01** governance - CODEOWNERS, PR/issue templates and branch-protection policy which E03 encodes as required checks.
- Downstream: **E04** observability and **E09** auth/RBAC are blocked on E03 (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§11.1).

## Branch
`feat/e03-cicd-<short>` per child (e.g. `feat/e03-cicd-skeleton`). PR size guidance: one workflow concern per PR, <= 400 LOC diff; workflow YAML changes must describe the resulting job graph in the PR body.

## Children dependency graph
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E02[E02 Monorepo] --> T01[E03-T01 Pipeline skeleton + resolver]
    E01[E01 Governance] --> T13[E03-T13 Branch protection + merge queue]
    E01 --> X01[E03-X01 STRIDE supply chain]
    T01 --> T02[E03-T02 JS lane]
    T01 --> T03[E03-T03 Python lane]
    T02 --> T04[E03-T04 Coverage gate]
    T03 --> T04
    T01 --> T05[E03-T05 Generated-code freshness]
    T02 --> T06[E03-T06 Contract/integration/e2e/a11y jobs]
    T03 --> T06
    X01 --> T07[E03-T07 Security scanning lane]
    T01 --> T07
    T07 --> T08[E03-T08 Image build + SBOM + cosign]
    T08 --> T09[E03-T09 Dev auto-deploy + gated staging]
    T03 --> T10[E03-T10 Alembic migration job]
    T10 --> T09
    T08 --> T11[E03-T11 Changelog + release job]
    T04 --> T13
    T06 --> T13
    T07 --> T13
    T13 --> T15[E03-T15 CI runbook + ADR-0013 validation]
    T05 --> Q01[E03-Q01 Gate verification + QA sign-off]
    T06 --> Q01
    T07 --> Q01
    T09 --> Q01
    T13 --> Q01
```
Deferred children (`K01`, `T12`, `T14`, `D01`, `D02`, `Q02`-`Q05`, `X02`-`X05`) are not shown: they are out of the
S01-S03 train per the Deferred scope table.

## Risks
| Risk | Handling |
|---|---|
| R2 Render performance (benchmark runner) | A single pinned GPU runner is a merge-blocking single point of failure; `E03-K01`/`E03-T14` define the architect-approved manual-override path (ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Consequences). |
| R5 Scope | Pipelines absorb unlimited polish; the first sizing pass hit 82 pts against a 42-pt allocation, which is why the Deferred scope table exists and is binding. Scope is fixed to the ADR-0013 job list, with nightly-only work isolated in `E03-T12`. |
| Supply-chain compromise (TB-8) | `E03-X01` STRIDE, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, OIDC, `--ignore-scripts`, signed images, gitleaks full-history. |
| CI cost/minutes | Path filters, concurrency cancellation, caching; measured weekly against the 15-minute budget. |

## References
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` - pipeline shape, binding rules 1-10, validation section
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0012-testing-pyramid.md` - offline deterministic CI, no live venue in CI
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§6 conventional commits, Ã‚Â§7 PR lifecycle & merge queue, Ã‚Â§8 hotfix, Ã‚Â§9 environment promotion
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` - per-Kind DoR/DoD
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` - test pyramid, tool table Ã‚Â§4, load Ã‚Â§8, security Ã‚Â§12
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§6.13 SR-130..SR-139, Ã‚Â§6.14 SR-140..SR-146, Ã‚Â§12.2 Semgrep `cv-*` rules, Ã‚Â§12.3 required checks
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` - axe-core merge gate, pa11y-ci sweep
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` - budgets #3, #4, #5, #13 and the k6/Locust harness spec
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3 changelog automation, Ã‚Â§4 release checklist, Ã‚Â§5 PRR
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§9 Alembic migrations, single-head rule, `alembic check` drift detection
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4 R0 goals/scope/exit criteria/quality gates, Ã‚Â§11.1 epic dependency graph


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Build the Actions PR skeleton with path filters and a checks resolver
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` chooses "GitHub Actions with path-filtered, parallel jobs". Binding rule 2 is the hard part: *"Path filtering decides which jobs run, but the required set is computed from the same filter so a skipped-but-required job reports success only when genuinely not applicable (a 'required checks resolver' job emits the conclusion)."* Without this, GitHub branch protection either blocks forever on skipped jobs or is satisfied by jobs that should have run. This Task lays the entry-point workflow every other E03 Task plugs lanes into.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml`: triggers `pull_request` (opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review) against `main`; top-level `permissions: contents: read`; `concurrency: group: pr-${{ github.head_ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true` (ADR-0013 rule 7).
- `changed-paths` job using `dorny/paths-filter` pinned by SHA, emitting boolean outputs: `js`, `py`, `engine`, `protocol`, `infra`, `docs`, `e2e`, `migrations`.
- Reusable-workflow skeletons `.github/workflows/_job-js.yml`, `_job-py.yml`, `_job-contract.yml`, `_job-security.yml`, `_job-e2e.yml`, `_job-engine-bench.yml` - each a `workflow_call` stub in this Task, filled in by T02/T03/T06/T07/T14.
- `ci-required` resolver job: `if: always()`, consumes `needs.*.result` plus the filter outputs, fails when an *applicable* lane is not `success`, succeeds when a lane is `skipped` **and** its filter output is `false`, and fails loudly ("gate misconfiguration") when a lane is `skipped` while its filter is `true`.
- Always-on jobs wired here: commitlint (conventional commits, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§6), licence-header check, docs link check (ADR-0013 pipeline shape line "[always]").
- `.github/actions-pins.md` documenting each pinned action SHA + its upstream tag, and a Dependabot entry for the `github-actions` ecosystem (SR-132, SR-134).
- `CODEOWNERS` entry making DevSecOps a code-owner of `.github/workflows/**`.

## Out of scope
- Any lane's actual commands (T02, T03, T06, T07, T14).
- Branch-protection configuration - T13 consumes `ci-required`.
- Post-merge, staging, nightly and release workflows (T08, T09, T11, T12).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Docs-only pull request skips code lanes yet reports green
  Given a pull request that changes only files under "docs/"
  When the pipeline runs
  Then the js, py, contract, e2e and engine lanes are skipped
  And commitlint, licence-header and docs-link jobs run
  And the "ci-required" job concludes success

Scenario: An applicable lane that is skipped fails the gate
  Given a pull request that changes "packages/chart-engine/src/renderer.ts"
  And the engine lane is disabled by a misconfigured condition so it reports skipped
  When the "ci-required" job evaluates results
  Then it fails with the message "gate misconfiguration: engine applicable but skipped"

Scenario: Superseded runs are cancelled
  Given a pull request with a run in progress
  When a new commit is pushed to the same head ref
  Then the in-progress run is cancelled by the concurrency group
  And only the newest run reports a conclusion

Scenario: An unpinned action is rejected
  Given a workflow file references "actions/checkout@v4" by tag
  When the workflow-lint step runs the SR-132 pin check
  Then the job fails naming the unpinned reference
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolver logic (pseudo-code, runs in `actions/github-script`):
```
LANES = {js: needs.js, py: needs.py, contract: needs.contract, e2e: needs.e2e,
         security: needs.security, engine: needs.engine, a11y: needs.a11y}
for name, lane in LANES:
    applicable = filters[name]
    if applicable and lane.result != 'success': fail(name + ' required and not successful')
    if not applicable and lane.result == 'skipped': continue
    if applicable and lane.result == 'skipped': fail('gate misconfiguration: ' + name)
```
- The pin check is a small script (`tools/ci/check_action_pins.py`) grepping `uses:` lines for a 40-hex SHA; it also asserts no workflow uses `pull_request_target` (SR-132).
- Config keys: repository variables `CV_CI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (default 20), `CV_CI_DEBUG` (never enables `set -x` around secrets, SR-146).
- Error codes surfaced in the resolver summary: `CI-GATE-001` applicable lane failed, `CI-GATE-002` gate misconfiguration, `CI-GATE-003` unpinned action.

## Test plan
- Unit: pytest for `tools/ci/check_action_pins.py` - pinned SHA passes, tag fails, `pull_request_target` fails, comment lines ignored.
- Unit: node test for the resolver matrix over all (applicable x result) combinations, including `cancelled` and `failure`.
- Integration: `act`-free approach - three fixture PRs in a scratch branch (docs-only, python-only, engine-only) with the resulting conclusions recorded in the ticket.
- Coverage target: >=85% for `tools/ci` (Python package threshold).

## Security notes
- SR-132: SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege `permissions`, `pull_request_target` prohibited - all three enforced by the pin-check step added here.
- SR-146: workflows must not `set -x` around secret usage or dump environment; a lint rule greps for `env | ` and `set -x` in workflow run blocks.
- Threat: a malicious PR modifying a workflow to exfiltrate secrets - mitigated because PR workflows receive no secrets (ADR-0013 rule 6) and `.github/workflows/**` is CODEOWNER-gated.
- Data classification: no secrets touched by this Task.

```gherkin
  Given a pull request introducing "const x: number = 'a'" in "packages/ui"
```

body:
## Context

- **Pytest network guard**: enforce ADR-0012's rule that "no test may contact `api.bybit.com` or the live WS" - a `conftest.py` autouse fixture patching socket creation to reject non-loopback connections, plus a CI-level assertion that the `exchange_smoke` marker is deselected.
- Import-linter contract execution (`ADR-0004`), reported as its own check `architecture`.

- Postgres/QuestDB service containers for the subset of tests marked `integration_db`, pinned by digest (SR-131).

- Timeouts: 20 min; `-p no:randomly` is **not** used - test order randomisation stays on, with the seed printed for reproduction.

title: Enforce coverage thresholds as a blocking CI gate
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4 makes coverage a gate with a stated behaviour: ">=85% backend & engine packages, >=80% frontend (**enforced, build fails below**)". `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§3.2 additionally requires "no regression to package baseline" - a per-package ratchet, not just a floor. `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 names `coverage-thresholds` as a required check on `main`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-coverage.yml` consuming the coverage artifacts produced by `E03-T02` (lcov per JS package) and `E03-T03` (coverage.xml for `services/api`).
- `tools/ci/coverage_gate.py`: reads `tools/ci/coverage-baselines.json` (package -> {floor, baseline}) and fails when `measured < floor` or `measured < baseline - tolerance` (tolerance 0.5 pp to absorb line-count noise).
- Floors seeded per the standard: `services/api` 85, `packages/chart-engine` 85, `packages/protocol` 85, `packages/ui` 80, `apps/app-web` 80, `apps/app-electron` 80.
- Baseline-raise automation: when a package's measured coverage exceeds its baseline by >=1 pp on `main`, a bot PR raises the baseline (ratchet up, never down).
- Baseline **lowering** requires an explicit commit editing `coverage-baselines.json` with a `Reason:` line, CODEOWNER approval from the QA lead - enforced by a CODEOWNERS rule on that file.
- A PR-comment summary table (package, floor, baseline, measured, delta, verdict) with words not colours.

## Out of scope
- Writing tests to reach the thresholds (owned by each feature epic).
- Mutation testing and flakiness quarantine (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A package below its floor fails the build
  Given "services/api" measures 83.2% line coverage
  When the coverage gate runs
  Then the job fails with "services/api 83.2% < floor 85.0%"

Scenario: A regression against baseline fails even when above the floor
  Given "packages/ui" has baseline 91.0% and measures 88.0%
  When the coverage gate runs
```

## Context
ADR-0013 binding rule 3: *"Generated-code freshness is a hard gate. `packages/protocol` is regenerated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema; any diff fails the build. Generated files are committed so consumers need no codegen step."* `ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md` reinforces it: *"Binary framing is unforgiving of drift. Mitigated by the `version` byte, a CI check that regenerates `packages/protocol` and fails on a diff, and fuzz tests feeding malformed frames to the decoder."* ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Validation requires a deliberate "break the protocol" PR during Sprint 01 to prove the gate bites - executed under `E03-T15`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-gen.yml`, always-on (the contract sources may change from any lane).
- Step: `make gen && git diff --exit-code -- packages/protocol` per ADR-0013's literal wording, plus `git status --porcelain` to catch *untracked* generated files that `git diff` would miss.
- Sources wired: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (REST models/clients) and the WS schema definitions of `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (topic envelopes, snapshot/delta frames, binary framing constants).
- Failure output: the actual unified diff rendered in the job summary plus the exact reproduction command (`make gen`), so a contributor never has to guess.
- A deterministic-generation assertion: `make gen` twice in a row must produce a byte-identical tree (catches map-ordering nondeterminism, which would make the gate flaky and therefore ignored).
- Codegen toolchain versions pinned in `Makefile`/`tools/gen/requirements.txt`; a version bump that changes output must be a deliberate, reviewed commit.

## Out of scope
- Contract *conformance* tests (server actually matching the schema) - `E03-T06`.
- Authoring the protocol schema itself - `E17` (WS protocol epic) and the API epics.
- Fuzz tests of the decoder - owned by the engine/protocol epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An in-sync tree passes
  Given "packages/protocol" matches the output of "make gen"
  When the freshness job runs
  Then "git diff --exit-code" succeeds and the job passes

Scenario: A schema edit without regeneration fails
  Given a pull request adds a field to a schema in "docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml"
  And "packages/protocol" is unchanged
  When the freshness job runs
  Then the job fails and the job summary shows the missing generated diff and the command "make gen"

Scenario: Untracked generated output fails
  Given "make gen" produces a new file that is not committed and is git-ignored by mistake
  When the freshness job runs
  Then "git status --porcelain" is non-empty and the job fails

Scenario: Non-deterministic generation is caught
  Given the generator emits map keys in a non-deterministic order
  When "make gen" runs twice and the outputs are compared
  Then the job fails with "codegen is not deterministic" before any diff check is reported
```

## Technical notes / design
- Order matters: determinism check first, then freshness - otherwise a flaky generator presents as a random freshness failure and erodes trust in the gate.
- The job runs on a clean checkout with no cache to prevent a stale cached artifact masking drift.
- Error codes: `CI-GEN-001` drift, `CI-GEN-002` untracked output, `CI-GEN-003` non-deterministic generation, `CI-GEN-004` generator toolchain version mismatch.

- Coverage: N/A (workflow + Makefile target); the generator's own tests belong to E02/E17.

## Security notes
- Generated-code drift is a correctness *and* security issue: the chart engine decodes binary frames and SR-128 requires bounds-checked decoding driven by the generated constants. Drift between generator and consumer is exactly the state SR-128 assumes cannot happen.
- The job needs `contents: read` only; no secrets.

## Scope / Deliverables

title: Automate dev deploy and add a gated staging deploy with rollback
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 2 requires "a green pipeline from commit to dev deployment" with no manual step, and `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§9 defines three environments - dev (docker compose on WSL Ubuntu, tip of `main`), staging (= Bybit demo), prod (= live) - with promotion gates. ADR-0013 rule 8 makes deployment image-based and immutable and makes production "a deliberate, checklisted action". This Task delivers dev auto-deploy and the *gated* staging deploy job; prod promotion remains a checklisted human action per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/main.yml` deploy stage: after a successful signed build, deploy to dev by **digest**, verifying the cosign signature immediately before applying (`E03-T08` threat closure).
- Deployment mechanism: a self-hosted runner on the dev host executing `docker compose -f compose.dev.yml up -d --wait` against a rendered compose file with the pinned digest; no SSH keys held in GitHub (the runner is inside the trust boundary).
- Post-deploy smoke test: `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` (paths per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`) and the build-info endpoint asserting the deployed git sha equals the just-built sha - the single most common silent-failure mode is "deploy succeeded, old image still running".
- `.github/workflows/staging.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` + release-branch trigger, bound to a GitHub Environment `staging` with **required reviewers** and a deployment branch policy restricting it to `main`/`release/*` (SR-141 environment protection).
- Staging smoke: health checks, WS connect, and the `@demo-rest-only` E2E subset job registration from `E03-T06` (empty in R0, mandatory from R3).
- Rollback: `workflow_dispatch` input `rollback_to_digest`; documented procedure re-deploying the previous digest with **no down-migration** (ADR-0013 rule 9, expand/contract).
- Deployment records: every deploy appends to `deployments/ledger.jsonl` (sha, digest, environment, actor, timestamp, outcome) committed by the workflow for auditability until E04's observability lands.

## Out of scope
- Prod/live deployment and the Live-enablement gate (R4, `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§6).
- Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager (`E04`).
- Feature-flag service implementation (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§10.4 assigns the flag *service* to infra, delivered in a later epic); this Task only ensures deploys do not reset flag state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Merge to main auto-deploys to dev
  Given a signed image for commit "abc1234" exists
  When the deploy stage runs
  Then the dev stack is updated to that image digest
  And the build-info endpoint reports git sha "abc1234"
  And the deployment ledger gains a success entry

Scenario: An unsigned or tampered image is refused
  Given an image whose cosign signature does not verify
  When the deploy stage attempts to apply it
  Then deployment aborts before any container is replaced
  And the ledger records a "signature-verification-failed" entry

Scenario: Staging requires a named reviewer
  Given the staging deploy workflow is dispatched
  When it reaches the "staging" environment gate
  Then it waits for approval from a required reviewer
  And it is cancelled automatically after the configured wait timer without deploying

Scenario: Rollback restores the previous digest without a down-migration
  Given the current dev deployment is digest D2 and the previous was D1
  When the rollback workflow is dispatched with "rollback_to_digest=D1"
  Then D1 is redeployed and the smoke test passes
  And no Alembic down-migration is executed

Scenario: A failed smoke test marks the deployment failed
  Given the deployed container fails "/health/ready" for 60 seconds
  When the smoke step times out
  Then the job fails, the ledger records the failure, and the previous digest is automatically restored
```

## Technical notes / design
- Auto-rollback on smoke failure is deliberate for **dev only**; staging failures alert and stop, because a half-rolled-back staging environment during a soak (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§4.2) is harder to reason about than a stopped one.
- Migrations run on boot under an advisory lock (ADR-0013 rule 9) - delivered by `E03-T10`; the deploy step waits for the migration to report completion before smoke-testing.
- Environment variables and non-secret settings come from a committed `.env.example`-derived render; **no exchange secret ever enters CI** (SR-140, SR-144).
- Error codes: `CI-DEP-001` signature verification failed, `CI-DEP-002` smoke failed, `CI-DEP-003` sha mismatch after deploy, `CI-DEP-004` migration lock timeout.

## Test plan
- Integration: five fixture runs, one per scenario, including a deliberately tampered image and a container forced to fail readiness.
- Chaos: kill the dev host runner mid-deploy and assert the ledger and stack converge to a known state on the next run (feeds the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).
- E2E: staging smoke path executed once end-to-end with a real approval.
- Coverage: deploy helper scripts under `tools/ci` >=85%.

## Security notes
- SR-141: staging is a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers; the self-hosted dev runner is inside the trust boundary and holds no GitHub secrets beyond its registration token.
- SR-140: **no production Bybit credentials in CI** - the dev and staging stacks obtain demo credentials from the host's envelope-encrypted store, not from GitHub secrets.
- Signature verification at deploy time closes the tamper-in-transit path opened between build and run.
- Threat: a compromised self-hosted runner deploying arbitrary images - mitigated by digest+signature verification, restricted runner labels, and an ephemeral workspace.
- Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no product UI. The deployment ledger and job summaries are text-based and screen-reader friendly.

## Performance notes
Deploy + smoke target <= 3 min so the full commit-to-dev path stays inside R0's 15-minute exit criterion together with the build.

## Observability

title: Add the Alembic migration job with single-head, drift and expand/contract checks
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§9 states the rules: Alembic 1.13+ over SQLAlchemy 2.0 async metadata; *"Single linear history on `main` (no branching heads). `alembic heads` must return exactly one revision - enforced in CI"*; and schema drift is detected by comparing `alembic upgrade head` against `models.py` via `alembic check`. ADR-0013 rule 9 adds the operational constraint: *"Migrations are applied on boot under an advisory lock and must be backward-compatible for one release (expand/contract), so a rollback never requires a down-migration."* Two engineers branching migrations in the same sprint is the default outcome without this gate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-migrations.yml`, applicable when the `migrations` path filter is true (`services/api/**/alembic/**`, `services/api/**/models.py`).
- Checks: (1) `alembic heads` returns exactly one revision; (2) `alembic check` reports no drift between `models.py` and head; (3) `alembic upgrade head` succeeds from an empty database; (4) `alembic upgrade head` succeeds from the **previous release tag's** schema (upgrade-path test, not just greenfield); (5) `IF NOT EXISTS` is absent from migration files (`21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§: "`IF NOT EXISTS` is never used in migrations - Alembic owns state").
- **Expand/contract lint**: a migration containing a destructive operation (`drop_column`, `drop_table`, non-nullable `add_column` without a server default, type narrowing) must carry an explicit `# cv:contract-phase: <release>` annotation justifying it; otherwise the job fails. This mechanically enforces ADR-0013 rule 9.
- Boot-time advisory-lock application helper (`services/api` startup path) asserted by an integration test: two concurrent boots must serialise, with the loser waiting rather than racing.
- The migration job also runs in `main.yml` before the deploy stage so a bad migration never reaches a running environment (`E03-T09` dependency).

## Out of scope
- Writing the actual schema/migrations (owned by `E07` and each feature epic).
- QuestDB table definitions and Parquet layout drift checks (`E07`) - noted here so the boundary is explicit.
- Data backfills and retention jobs (`E07`, `E16`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Two migration heads block the merge
  Given two branches each added a migration from the same parent revision
  When both are merged and "alembic heads" is evaluated
  Then the job fails with "expected 1 head, found 2" and names both revisions

Scenario: Model drift is detected
  Given a column is added to "models.py" without a corresponding migration
  When "alembic check" runs
  Then the job fails describing the drifted table and column

Scenario: A destructive migration without a contract annotation fails
  Given a migration calls "op.drop_column" with no "cv:contract-phase" annotation
  When the expand/contract lint runs
  Then the job fails citing ADR-0013 rule 9

Scenario: Upgrade from the previous release succeeds
  Given a database restored to the schema of the previous release tag
  When "alembic upgrade head" runs
  Then it completes successfully with no manual intervention

Scenario: Concurrent boots serialise on the advisory lock
  Given two api containers start simultaneously against one database
  When both attempt to apply migrations
  Then exactly one applies them and the other waits and then starts normally
```

## Technical notes / design
- Upgrade-path test uses a schema snapshot artifact published at each release tag (`schema/<tag>.sql`), restored into a throwaway Postgres service container.
- Advisory lock: `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('cv_migrations'))` held for the duration of `upgrade head`, released on completion; a configurable `CV_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 300 s) turns a deadlock into a clear `CI-DEP-004`/startup error instead of a hang.
- Error codes: `CI-MIG-001` multiple heads, `CI-MIG-002` drift, `CI-MIG-003` destructive without annotation, `CI-MIG-004` upgrade-path failure, `CI-MIG-005` `IF NOT EXISTS` used.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=85%): the expand/contract lint over fixture migration files (destructive annotated, destructive unannotated, additive, ambiguous batch operations).
- Integration: a throwaway Postgres service container exercising greenfield upgrade, previous-release upgrade, and the concurrent-boot advisory-lock scenario.
- Contract: `alembic check` treated as the contract between `models.py` and the migration chain.
- Coverage target: >=85% for the lint tool and the startup helper.

## Security notes
- Migrations touch `api_keys` and audit tables in later epics; SR-tagged note per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§4.1: any migration touching `api_keys` must preserve envelope encryption at rest - the lint flags such migrations for mandatory Security review by matching table names in `tools/ci/security-sensitive-tables.txt`.
- Append-only audit tables (E09) must never be altered destructively; they are listed as forbidden targets for `drop_*` regardless of annotation.
- CI uses ephemeral throwaway databases only; no production data, ever.

Migration job target <= 3 min. Long-running migrations are a deploy-latency risk; the lint warns when a migration adds an index without `CONCURRENTLY` on a table listed as large in `21-database-schema.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/changelog.yml`: on merge to `main`, parses conventional commits since the last tag and updates the `## Unreleased` section of `/CHANGELOG.md` via a bot commit.

- Security-fix wording guard: entries under `Security` must not include exploit detail; a lint warns on lines containing CVE proof-of-concept markers or the words "exploit"/"payload", pointing the author to the internal finding tracker.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: on `release/*` branch or a `vX.Y.Z` tag - compute the semver bump, finalise the Unreleased section under the version heading with the release date, draft the GitHub Release with that section as the body, attach SBOMs (`E03-T08`), and build + sign Electron installers.
- **`1.0.0` guard**: the workflow refuses to produce a `1.0.0` tag unless a `RELEASE_ALLOW_1_0_0=true` input is explicitly supplied, encoding the "declared explicitly, not automatically" rule.
- Release-checklist automation: the workflow opens a release-checklist issue from a template containing `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§4 items, and refuses to publish a non-draft release while the PRR gate item is unchecked.
- Signed tags: release tags require signed commits (`04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 branch protection note).

```gherkin
  Then the check fails asking for a conventional title or a Changelog footer

Scenario: A breaking change forces a MAJOR bump proposal
  Given a commit since the last tag contains a "BREAKING CHANGE:" footer
  When the release workflow computes the next version
  Then it proposes a MAJOR bump and states the triggering commit

Scenario: 1.0.0 cannot be produced accidentally
  Given the computed bump from 0.9.x would be MAJOR
  When the release workflow runs without "RELEASE_ALLOW_1_0_0=true"
  Then it fails with "1.0.0 requires explicit Live-enablement declaration"

Scenario: A docs-only PR is exempt
  Given a pull request titled "docs: fix typo in sitemap"

```

- Version state lives in the git tags plus a `version.txt` written at release time, so no package file is the source of truth in a polyglot monorepo (backend + frontend + Electron ship together per `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§2).

This ticket is the black-box test plan for E03 as a whole: for every required check, a deliberately-broken fixture PR that **must** fail, plus a clean fixture PR that **must** pass - because a gate that fails everything is as useless as one that fails nothing.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Positive control: a clean no-op PR that must pass every applicable check, proving the gates are not failing indiscriminately.
- Execution record: each case run, with the run URL, the observed error code and PASS/FAIL of the *expectation*.
- Exploratory charter (timeboxed 4 h): "Can I get code onto `main`, or into a deployed image, without passing the gates?" - attempts include renaming a job so a required check vanishes, merging while a check is queued, editing workflows in the same PR being gated, force-push attempts, and bypassing via the release bot's allowance.

- Runner health-check + alert and a documented fallback path for when the GPU runner is unavailable, closing the accepted-risk items A5/G3 in `docs/plan/threat-models/E03-supply-chain.md` section 5.
- Dependency mirroring / retry-with-backoff for PyPI/npm/GHCR registries to reduce A5/R4 (registry outage blocking merges).

## Out of scope
- Authoring the engine benchmarks themselves (B1-B10) — that is E06/E11's scope; this ticket provides the runner and comparison harness only.
- Full VM-per-job isolation of the GPU runner — that is `E03-K01`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A PR outside chart-engine/** does not require the GPU runner
  Given a pull request touching only "services/api"
  When the required-checks resolver runs

Scenario: A registry timeout produces a clear failure, not a silent hang
  Given a fixture simulating a PyPI/npm/GHCR timeout during install
  When the affected CI job runs
  Then it fails within a bounded timeout with a clear error message naming the registry

Scenario: GPU runner unavailability is surfaced, not silently retried forever
  Given the self-hosted GPU runner is offline or contended
  When a chart-engine PR's benchmark job is scheduled
  Then a health-check alert fires and the documented fallback path is followed
```
